key_insight: This paper shows that a unified multimodal model can improve both visual understanding and image generation without human labels by teaching itself through internal self-consistency rewards. In simple terms: the model asks questions, solves them, and uses the agreement between answers and generated content as training signal.
problem_solved: Most unified large multimodal models depend on curated supervision such as annotations, preference labels, or external reward models. This work tackles the challenge of improving both understanding and generation using only unlabeled images, reducing reliance on expensive human feedback.
method: Uses a self-evolving framework with three internal roles: Proposer, Solver, and Generator.
The Proposer creates visual questions from unlabeled images to drive learning.
The Solver answers these questions and checks consistency, producing self-consistency rewards.
The Generator uses these rewards to refine image generation and support unified multimodal learning.
impact: For practitioners, this suggests a path toward cheaper and more scalable multimodal training pipelines that reduce dependence on labeled data and external reward models. It can make unified models easier to adapt in data-scarce or annotation-expensive settings.

paper_title: Ask, Solve, Generate: Self-Evolving Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation via Self-Consistency Rewards
paper_authors: Ritesh Thawkar, Shravan Venkatraman, Omkar Thawakar, Abdelrahman Shaker, Fahad Khan
